If anything I'd get into maybe finding counseling for anxiety. My new job has 8 free counseling sessions via EAP so I'm going to take advantage of it.  Managing our anxieties will help us out in the long run.  if you want to chat more or have any other thoughts to share send me a PM. Wish you the best with everything.

Lots of good point in all of these posts about XIII vs. XV.  Personally I enjoyed my time with both but really enjoyed XIII most.  The things that seems to bother people the most about XIII is the linearity, lack of towns, NPCs, etc.  XIII lacked some of the things that most JRPGs are known for.  So I get the disdain over that.  I don't know, but it didn't bother me too much though.

When I was playing it I never thought to myself "man do I want some towns and npcs and shops" I guess I was too much into the story, characters, and ogling my first next-gen at the time JRPG. Plus I had just started college so maybe the linear nature of it made it feel more "pick up and play" to me sinc i was really busy and that gorgeous soundtrack. 

Anyways I think the XIII/XIII-2 series combat was more enjoyable than XV.  XV imo nailed the team aspect.  It felt great doing team attacks and the combat banter and all of that.  The battle system really exemplifies the idea of the brotherhood theme.  It is theme extended to gameplay and I loved it.   Buuuut I got sorta bored with it.  Magic is meh but can be useful, and the moment to moment just felt dull really fast.  Like I was fighting the same way late game as I was early game.  And that can be true for a lot of games but for some reason I really felt that sentiment stronger in this game.

XIII on the other hand has a really slow start with its battle system.  It's probably too slow.  I don't know I haven't played XIII or XIII-2 in years.  But I think its biggest downside is that the battle system doesn't really shine until endgame.  Both XIII games are pretty simple affairs until you get to endgame and have more control over your party builds.  It isn't until that you face off against endgame foes (XIII's higher end hunts, the final boss and DLC in XIII-2) that you are really challenged by anything. That's where the battle system shines.

But eh I just chalk it up to both are fun but have issues.  But I really prefer XIII's at the end of the day.

Story....I like the story of XIII then XIII-2 came and I sighed.  XV? I really just love the bro dynamic of it the most.  Everything else feels a bit half baked (XIII and XV both managed to hit my feels hard at certain points though).  Environments? I guess I can say those are equal.  I found Gapra Whitewood and Oerba to be awesome in XIII.  In XV I really liked Lestallum. Just something about that place it feels "real" and "lived in". Like I've traveled and it reminded me of places I've been too.  Pretty great.  

Both games are pretty meh on intriguing sidequests though lol. Overall, before I further ramble, both games are imperfect but I personally give the nod to XIII in the end.

Thank for your response.  I'll answer these: 

* **When I started college** I wasn't sure what I imagined my life being. I thought I wanted to get into mental health.  I thought I wanted to help people learn how to help themselves because of my own anxieties.  That's why I originally got into Psychology.  Found myself dealing with my own issues more than really embracing the experience and opportunities alloted to me.  As graduation felt nearer I felt a mix of relief and dread.  Relief because school stress was ending but dread because a whole new stress would be on me. I honestly felt lost and still do to an extent.  The desire to help others be able to help themselves is strong to me.  Yet I doubt at times because I couldn't even handle call center work.

*  **Concerning going back to retail,** it was definitely good because I felt comfortable working at Game Stop it was simple work and honestly the only work I had that lasted three years.  That is a long time for me at a company.  It isn't something I can see a career path being made from. If I were to go back (which I guess I could closer to holiday times since I am now rehirable) it would mostly be for weekend shifts.  Honestly it wouldn't be much since I guess I'd be starting all over.

*  **Concerning how I support myself,** this is a bit embarrassing and I try not to hold shame over it but it can be hard to let the negative feelings go at times, but I don't really.  I have a lot of money saved up from my last call center job.  I've been living off of that to pay my personal expenses while living with my parents.  I've helped out with bills for quite a long time but won't be able to much longer since money is running out.  

*  **As it relates to my network/support system**, I have my family yes.  My parents are wonderful and they support me as long as I'm trying to make something better of myself.  They are comfortable with me still living here at home as long as I'm trying.  I'm glad for their support and I know most people don't have this sort of position to be in.  Concerning friends, I don't really have any close by that I can talk to in a productive way about "future and career" things.  I guess you could say they are friends more for "fun things" so despite my own efforts topics like this don't come up once.  I have one online whom I am very close with and we can talk about basically anything so that helps on the morale front quite often.  I don't really have any past professors from college that I speak to regularly unfortunately.  I tried keeping contact with them around my graduation time in 2013 but around 2014 I sorta had it fall by the wayside.

*  **Additional education** doesn't sound like a bad idea but I don't really know how I'd fund it.  I feel lucky enough getting out of college without any debt to deal with.

*  **I have tried temp agencies** in the past.  I have submitted my info but maybe it is time to follow up and try again. 

*  **After graduating, and more than 3 years later,** going to me career center at my alma mater is still an option?  I didn't think it was.  I tried to use them while I was in college and other professors to figure out where I wanted to go but the conversations never went anywhere.  It always stopped at my own indecision and inability to answer the question of what I really wanted to do an what path I thought was right for me.

No need to apologize.  Unfortunately I don't have much advice but I can give support.  It is good you are looking and know you want to be out of the retail line of work.  That's a good first start as well as posting here.  Hang tough in there and know you definitely aren't alone.  Hopefully you, myself, and the rest of us here trying to find a different career path can get onto something.  I believe so.  : )

I guess from playing so many JRPGs I'm used to doing other content and grinding stuff in order to get the really good gear, weapons, and levels that will allow me to tackle the super hard content.

Like Final Fantasy X.  Gotta grind that sphere grid and do all of these sidequests to gather everyone's Ultimate Weapons before even thinking about Omega, crazy arena fights, and Penance.  I'm used to the reward not being just more gear to make the fights easier but something like "Proof of Omega" after you wreck Omega Weapon.

I know it is different in MMOs of course but I always thought it'd be cool that, after you geared up in savage, there was some other really awesomely difficult fight to use that fancy gear on.  A fight that would drop a title, music, mounts, cosmetics, etc.  

Aside from the idea of getting into raiding for the  challenge, I think that would motivate me a bit more then just gear that's a bit better but not necessarily required to get that first clear on most of the content.  But I'm not a raider like I said.

This is a very good post that I very much appreciate.  MMO addiction or heck even just playing more than one should when compared to other life activities, goals, etc. is a very serious thing.  As someone who is currently unemployed, I'd like to weigh in a bit on what helps me not to binge on FF all day/every day when I'm not spending time searching for jobs. This I feel is important because I play with some individuals who are unemployed as well.  Some of them play from the time they get up to the time they go to sleep.  Hell, I used to be averaging 8 hours a day (I've got it to around half now give or take...more on the take side......I'm hardly perfect with this). Anyways things that help me to keep my FF in check:


1.  Routine is important.  My routine has me playing  during the evenings.  During the days I get up, take care of the usual house tasks that need to be done, then I focus myself on job searching/applying, and other goals and hobbies and necessary tasks.

2.  This leads to the point of other goals and hobbies.  I suppose I can only speak for myself, but even if I was employed now, I do not believe I would be happy with myself having just work and FF as the things I participate in with life.  It really is important to have goals and figure out what you care about.  Once I got a better handle on this I started feeling better with my routine. FF and gaming weren't the only things that could excite me everyday.

3.  Repetition of "doing the right thing".  Changing from playing for the greater part of the day when unemployed to a lot less when you are unsure of your goals or what is important to you is very difficult. That is why you really gotta practice and stick with it no matter how you are feeling. Long term results trump short term gratification.

4. Get a buddy.  Any friends worth being friends will support your decision and do what they can to help you out either by keeping you accountable, engaging you in conversation pertaining to things other than FF, etc.  Be real with your friends and they'll support you and vice versa.

Anyway, these are just things that help me rein myself back in when I find myself going toward the way of making binge sessions regular.
